guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting to TCU’s loss at UCF or Baylor’s win over Colorado as if either result settles this matchup. Our numbers give TCU more credit because its defense allowed only 264.8 yards per game through four games and held opponents to a 24.5 percent conversion rate on third down. That matters against a Baylor passing offense whose raw yardage was productive but whose efficiency profile has been less convincing.

The concern for us is how TCU sustains offense. Its rushing efficiency runs directly into the stronger part of Baylor’s defense, potentially putting more of the game on Jaden Craig. Craig produced three 300-yard passing games in his first four starts, but his two interceptions at UCF show the downside when volume does not become points.

That leaves us with a real but modest disagreement with the market. We can make a football case for TCU staying competitive, especially if its defense controls third down, but the difficult rushing matchup and reliance on Craig create enough volatility that the available price does not justify a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, the matchup to watch is TCU’s pass protection against Baylor’s pressure. Baylor averaged 3.75 sacks and 9.0 tackles for loss through four games, while TCU had already allowed nine sacks. Craig has spread the ball around—completing passes to at least six receivers in every game—but he needs enough time for that distribution to matter.

If Baylor consistently forces long-yardage situations, TCU’s ability to create scoring opportunities may not translate into finished drives. If TCU protects Craig, we think its passing game has enough variety to explain why our view is more favorable to the road team than the market’s.

recent_game.fact: Baylor defeated Colorado 23-13 on Sept. 26 to improve to 3-1 overall and 1-0 in Big 12 play.
Baylor held Colorado to 363 total yards, forced punts on eight of 15 drives, recovered a fumble and made two fourth-down stops.
Baylor recorded five sacks and 13 tackles for loss against Colorado; the 13 tackles for loss were its most since a 2019 win at Kansas State.
Linebacker Travion Barnes recorded a Baylor career-high nine tackles and two tackles for loss against Colorado.
DJ Lagway threw two touchdown passes in Baylor's win over Colorado.

opponent_notes.fact: At the time of these notes, TCU was 2-2 and coming off a 21-13 loss at UCF on Sept. 26.

quarterback.fact: Junior quarterback DJ Lagway transferred from Florida after making 19 starts in two seasons and throwing for 4,179 yards and 28 touchdowns.
Lagway suffered a lower-leg injury in the season opener against Auburn but played through it and finished 27-of-54 for 333 yards and two touchdowns.
Nate Bennett made his first career start against Prairie View A&M while filling in for Lagway and completed 24 of 36 passes for 314 yards and three touchdowns, with an additional rushing touchdown.
Bennett again relieved Lagway against Louisiana Tech and completed 21 of 24 passes for 253 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown.

offensive_personnel.fact: Baylor added 16 offensive players through the transfer portal for 2026, including quarterback DJ Lagway and offensive linemen Logan Moore, Nate Kibble, Asher Hale and Cole Rhett.
Baylor had seven first-time Bears starters on offense against Auburn: DJ Lagway, Dawson Pendergrass, Louis Brown IV, Gavin Freeman, Nate Kibble, Asher Hale and Logan Moore.
Center Harrison Cluff made his first Baylor start against Prairie View A&M, and right tackle Cooper Lovelace made his first Baylor start against Louisiana Tech.
Baylor entered 2026 needing to replace four offensive-line starters. Returning tackle Kaden Sieracki had started all 12 games in 2025, played 948 snaps and did not allow a sack.
Gavin Freeman, a transfer from Oklahoma State and Oklahoma, had 35 catches for 364 yards through Baylor's first four games and led the nation with 8.75 receptions per game.
Baylor replaced its five leading pass catchers from the 2025 offense, including NFL departures Josh Cameron and tight end Michael Trigg.
Running back Dawson Pendergrass returned in 2026 after missing the 2025 season with a preseason season-ending injury.

defensive_personnel.fact: Baylor added 21 defensive players through the transfer portal for 2026, with major additions on the defensive line, at edge rusher and at safety.
Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman brought Kansas State defenders Ryan Davis, Daniel Cobbs and Colby McCalister with him to Baylor.
Baylor added JACK pass rushers Ryan Davis from Kansas State and Garrick Ponder from Southern Miss after finishing 2025 with 12 sacks and 48 tackles for loss.

Baylor's first-time defensive starters against Auburn were nose tackle Hosea Wheeler, JACK Ryan Davis, linebacker Travion Barnes, STAR Daniel Cobbs, safeties Devin Turner and Colby McCalister, and cornerback Devon Jordan.
Defensive tackle Traevon Mitchell made his first NCAA start in Baylor's win over Colorado.
Baylor entered 2026 replacing linebacker Keaton Thomas, who transferred to Ole Miss after consecutive 100-tackle seasons.

coaching_changes.fact: Dave Aranda stopped serving as Baylor's defensive play caller and inside-linebackers coach after two seasons and hired Joe Klanderman from Kansas State as defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Jake Spavital returned for his third season as Baylor's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

Baylor hired Jacori Greer as defensive-line coach and Jeremy Modkins as cornerbacks coach, while Austin Woods entered his first full season leading the offensive line after serving as interim coach for the final five games of 2025.
